# tgo

Package main provides the TGo command.

The command owns file output. The compiler returns file contents so callers can choose where to write them. This keeps command\-line policy out of the compiler API.

In\-place output keeps generated Go beside its TGo source. A separate output directory provides a complete emitted module. Matching file names preserve Go's test and platform selection rules. Unchanged files keep their existing contents on disk.

Language rules belong to the compiler. Command\-line options choose the source and destination; they do not change the meaning of a program.
